title: Replace a non-serializable event prop across the boundary
businessContext: Review a focused Next.js application change before it reaches production. The proposed file below contains the defect or unsupported assumption; external application services, where imported, are integration boundaries.
problemStatement: Review the proposed app/page.tsx change. Identify the incorrect framework assumption, propose a minimal corrected implementation, and provide evidence for the selected version scope and its 15/16 differences. Explain the interview variation after solving the base task. This is a framework code review: actual rendering, routing and cache behavior must be checked in a real Next.js build, not a browser function sandbox.
starterCode:
import Button from './button';
export default function Page(){ return <Button onClick={()=>console.log('clicked')} />; }

constraints: Preserve the stated user behavior and keep trust boundaries explicit.
Use the selected version’s documented API; do not suppress build/type failures to hide the defect.
Split the two files at the annotated boundary and build.
Confirm the button works after hydration.
Verify no sensitive object fields are included in the props payload.
candidateTasks: Add actionable line-level review comments explaining impact and correction.
Write the corrected file in the local IDE copy; split annotated companion files where instructed.
Record actual build/request/navigation evidence against the acceptance checks and compare version notes.
hints: An ordinary server-created callback cannot be serialized as a client event handler.
Split the two files at the annotated boundary and build.
alternativeApproaches: Do not reduce the RSC serialization contract to JSON-only folklore. React supports specific richer values; check its current supported types. Still prefer an intentional DTO and avoid arbitrary class instances or ordinary function props.
commonMistakes: Verifying only next dev when the behavior depends on production rendering or bundling.
Treating a visible UI state, matcher or TypeScript type as a substitute for server-side validation and authorization.
